context.process_name: Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices
context.objective: Document how we carry out Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It starts when cash proceeds are received or expected, a deal closes or a realization happens, or the client asks us to calculate or carry out a distribution. First, as the preparer on the capital activity team or Fund Team, I confirm the entity, deal, amount, whether cash is expected or actually received, and the requested payment date. Then I decide if it is a distribution-only event or a combined call-and-distribution, which we call a net event. I assign a second reviewer, list what we need from the client tax team, and link the work to the event calendar. If cash arrived without deal context, or client instructions conflict, I escalate and get written client identification before any modeling. Next I classify the proceeds: match cash to the portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account, and classify each piece as return of capital, realized gain, dividend or income, or another supported category.
Once you’ve classified each piece of proceeds, what do you do next?

Before leaving classification I check that total classified proceeds equal the amount being modeled and every component has support. If bank activity alone does not identify the deal or character, I stop calculations and get written client classification; I never decide it from the bank description. Then I update cumulative proceeds: start from the prior approved cumulative proceeds file, add current proceeds by classification, confirm prior distributions, remaining invested capital and cumulative contributions, and reconcile to the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank and partner-capital records. The second reviewer verifies this. If there is an unexplained difference, the waterfall calculation is paused until it is resolved or documented. After that, with the reviewer and client input, I document the fund waterfall rules from the LPA and side letters, confirm whole fund versus deal or tranche, confirm escrow or holdback treatment, and lock the rule set. If a rule is ambiguous, we pause and get written direction from the client or legal adviser; we never create a missing rule.
Once the waterfall rule set is locked, how do you calculate the distribution amounts under it?

I enter current proceeds into the controlled waterfall model in the capital activity workbook and apply return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual split in the approved order for that fund. I calculate limited partner and general partner allocations including any holdback. If the model shows the fund is not in a carry position, no cash carry is paid and I document the model result; the reviewer confirms. Then I check that allocated cash plus retained or held cash equals total proceeds. If that fails, or I get negative, residual or unexpected results, I stop, investigate, and get client or legal confirmation when the economics are unclear. Next comes tax: the client tax team or tax adviser provides or approves the taxable-income allocation, which can differ from cash. If the GP or another investor has taxable income without cash, and the governing documents permit, I calculate or add a tax distribution, kept as separate support, and get tax-team approval. If tax input is missing or conflicting, final economics are held.
How is any tax withholding handled in this workflow?

Using the client or tax-team withholding schedule, I identify every investor subject to withholding and the jurisdiction and rate, then apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base, or just incorporate the approved client schedule. Approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments go in separately. For each investor I calculate gross distribution, withholding and net cash, and gross minus withholding must equal net cash; schedule totals must reconcile to the model and the approved tax input. The second reviewer checks the result. For a net event, approved withholding goes into the call-and-distribution net calculation with separate support kept. If a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing, or the schedule is late or revised, I escalate to the client or tax adviser and we hold or recalculate the affected calculations, notices and payments until there is a versioned schedule and renewed approval. We never decide rate or jurisdiction ourselves. Then I apply the investor allocation rules to build the draft investor distribution schedule.
How do you apply the investor allocation rules when building the draft distribution schedule?

I confirm the allocation basis the governing terms require: commitment percentage, limited partner percentage, a deal-specific basis or another basis. Excel percentages alone are not authoritative. I use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations, calculate each investor's proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash, and reconcile investor totals to the fund-level waterfall and tax schedules; they must agree apart from documented rounding. If a difference is unexplained or a percentage is not supported, I pause. Then I populate the final summary tab used for notices and payment support. After that the second reviewer does the internal review: proceeds and roll-forward continuity, waterfall rules and formulas, carry, preferred return, tax distribution, holdback, tax and withholding inputs against approved schedules, investor totals and reconciliations, and the draft notice labels, breakdowns and footnotes. Comments are recorded and resolved; unresolved errors or source gaps go back to me, the client or the tax adviser. The reviewer must sign off before anything goes to the client.
After your sign-off, what happens when the draft goes to the client, and what must be approved before notices or payments proceed?

To be clear, the sign-off is the second reviewer's, not mine. Once cleared, I send the package to the client and flag every estimated, pending or late tax input. If the client changes timing, proceeds character, tax amounts, withholding or notice language, I incorporate the approved changes, recalculate, and repeat the reconciliations and review checks. Then I get final written client approval and lock the version used for notices, posting and payment; nothing is released or paid from an unapproved version. If a change arrives after an entry or payment, we follow the controlled correction process and get renewed approval. Then the reviewer and I merge investor data into the Word notice template, showing gross proceeds, components, transaction type, taxable income, withholding, net payment and footnotes, and reconcile every notice to the locked schedule with QA. I hand posting and payment support to the Fund Team and Treasury. They check bank holidays and cut-offs, record the general-ledger entry and send wires; Investor Services publishes notices. Payment or release is held for a notice mismatch, bank closure, invalid instructions or incomplete approval.
What confirms the distribution work is complete after notices and payments are handled?

After payments, the Fund Team or I do the closeout. We track withheld amounts separately from investor net payments and give supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority. Who owns remittance, the payment steps and due dates I do not know; it is not confirmed, and if the owner is unclear the role has to be assigned before closeout. We update investor capital accounts and contribution and distribution history, then cumulative proceeds history and carried-interest tracking. Then we reconcile actual wires, withholding held or remitted, general-ledger balances and the locked schedule: gross distribution must equal net investor cash plus withholding, with no unexplained difference. If there is unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference, we escalate immediately and closeout stops; it may need a correction or reposting. Last, client-specific uploads; for One Rock the Cobalt upload is due within two days of the event. It is finished when the reconciled post-distribution record and remittance support are retained.
What can go wrong for investors, the client, or the fund if a distribution error is not caught before payment or closeout?

capture.summary: After payments, the Fund Team or participant performs closeout, including reconciliation and escalation of unresolved issues. Completion requires retention of the reconciled record and remittance support; tax-remittance ownership, steps and due dates remain unconfirmed. One Rock has a two-day Cobalt upload deadline.
